name: Belfries of Belgium and France
description: Fifty-six town belfries scattered across northern France and Belgium, built between the 11th and 17th centuries, rise above market squares from Bruges to Arras. Unlike church steeples or lords' keeps, these towers belonged to the townspeople, housing bells, charters and watchmen. Their Romanesque, Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque forms mark the moment when prosperous towns won their independence.
